problem_statement: An ICMP response handler can be invoked for a packet whose IP family does not match the family the handler was registered for. When an ICMP context is registered to handle a specific address family (IPv4 or IPv6), an incoming packet of the other family that happens to carry the same ICMP type and code still triggers that handler. Expected: an ICMP handler registered for a given address family should only be called for packets of that family, so a malformed packet (e.g. an IPv4 packet carrying an ICMPv6 Echo-Request type, or an IPv6 packet carrying an ICMPv4 Echo-Request type) must not invoke the handler of the other family.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/net/icmp -s tests/net/icmp/net.icmp.preempt -s net.icmp.preempt -O twister-out --no-clean -W
